chunks: Hakim, Abu Hamid, Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali in Balkh told us, saying: Abd al-Mu'min ibn Khalaf told us, saying: Hasan ibn Mahran al-Isbahani in Baghdad told me, saying: Hasan ibn Hamza ibn Hammad ibn Bahram al-Farsi told me, saying: Abu al-Qasim ibn Aban al-Qazwini told us, from Abu Bakr al-Hadhali, from Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Basri, saying:

The Commander of the Believers, Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), ascended the pulpit and said: O people, mention my lineage. Let he who knows me mention my lineage, otherwise, I will mention my lineage by myself. I am Zaid ibn Abd-Manaf ibn Amer ibn Amr ibn Mughira ibn Zaid ibn Kilab. Then Ibn al-Kawwa' stood up to him and said: O you, we do not know for you any lineage except that you are Ali ibn Abi Talib ibn Abdul-Muttalib ibn Hashim ibn Abd-Manaf ibn Qusay ibn Kilab. Then he said to him: O ignoble, indeed, my father named me 'Zaid' by the name of his grandfather 'Qusay', and the name of my father is 'Abd-Manaf', then the kunya (nickname) overtook the name, and indeed, the name of Abdul-Muttalib is 'Amer', then the laqab (epithet) overtook the name, and the name of Hashim is 'Amr', then the laqab overtook the name, and the name of Abd-Manaf is 'Mughira', then the laqab overtook the name, and the name of Qusay is 'Zaid', then the Arabs named him jointly due to that he had gathered them from the farthest land to Mecca, then the laqab overtook the name. He said: For Abdul-Muttalib are ten names, among them are: Abdul-Muttalib, Shayba, and Amer.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Belieathers (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.ابْنُ الْكَوَّاء: Ibn al-Kawwa' (a companion who questioned the lineage)
key_terms.الْكُنْيَة: Kunya (nickname derived from father or son's name)

ai.seo_question: What is the full genealogical name of Imam Ali and how do his kunyas and laqabs relate to his personal names?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elucidates the distinction between personal names (ism), kunyas, and laqabs, demonstrating how titles like 'Hashim' and 'Abd al-Muttalib' originally served as individual names before becoming tribal epithets. This clarification underscores the scholarly tradition of precise genealogical verification (isnad) and highlights the linguistic evolution of Arab naming conventions, affirming his lineage as 'Zaid ibn Abd-Manaf' to honor his grandfather Qusay, whose name was also 'Zaid'.
